authoredSolutions.51: Statement I: modulo 7, \(25\equiv4,\;20\equiv6,\;8\equiv1,\;3\equiv3\). Then \(4^{13}\equiv4,\;6^{13}\equiv(-1)^{13}\equiv6,\;1^{13}=1,\;3^{13}\equiv3\), summing to \(14\equiv0\pmod7\), so I is true. Statement II: with \(a=7+4\sqrt3,\;b=7-4\sqrt3\), we have \(a+b=14,\;ab=1,\;0<b<1\). The integer \(N=a^{25}+b^{25}\) obeys \(s_n=14s_{n-1}-s_{n-2}\), which is even for every \(n\). Since \(0<b^{25}<1\), the integral part of \(a^{25}\) equals \(N-1\), an odd number, so II is true. Both statements are true.
authoredSolutions.52: The sum is \(S=\sum_{k=0}^{1000}x^k(1+x)^{1000-k}\), a geometric series with ratio \(\frac{x}{1+x}\). Summing gives \(S=(1+x)^{1001}-x^{1001}\). The coefficient of \(x^{499}\) is \(\binom{1001}{499}\) and of \(x^{500}\) is \(\binom{1001}{500}\). Their sum is \(\binom{1001}{499}+\binom{1001}{500}=\binom{1002}{500}\).

authoredSolutions.55: With \(n=\tfrac2\theta\to\infty\), \(x^{2/\theta}=(x^2)^{1/\theta}\to0\) for \(|x|<1\) and \(\to\infty\) for \(|x|>1\). Near \(x=1\): for \(x<1,\;f=\cos\pi x\to-1\); for \(x>1,\;f\to-\frac{\sin(x-1)}{x-1}\to-1\); and \(f(1)=-1\), so \(f\) is continuous at \(1\) and (I) is false. Near \(x=-1\): the right limit is \(-1\), the left limit is \(-\tfrac{\sin2}{2}\), and \(f(-1)=1-\sin2\); these differ, so \(f\) is discontinuous at \(-1\) and (II) is false. Neither (I) nor (II) is true.

authoredSolutions.58: Statement I: \(f(x)=\tfrac{x}{1+|x|}\) is increasing on \(x\ge0\) and on \(x<0\) and is continuous, hence strictly increasing on \(\mathbb{R}\) and one-one — true. Statement II: \(f(x)=\tfrac{x^2+4x-30}{x^2-8x+18}\) has denominator \((x-4)^2+2>0\), is defined on all of \(\mathbb{R}\), and tends to \(1\) as \(x\to\pm\infty\) while non-constant, so it is not injective — many-one, true. Both statements are true.

authoredSolutions.63: Over \((-\tfrac\pi2,\tfrac\pi2)\), \([\sin x]+[\cos x]=-1\) on \((-\tfrac\pi2,0)\) (denominator \(2\)) and \(=0\) on \((0,\tfrac\pi2)\) (denominator \(3\)). Splitting by \([x]\) over \([-\tfrac\pi2,-1),[-1,0),[0,1),[1,\tfrac\pi2]\), the integrand is \(6,12,12,16\). Hence the integral \(=6(\tfrac\pi2-1)+12+12+16(\tfrac\pi2-1)=11\pi+2.\)

The odd powers at \(x=3\) and \(x=-12\) give sign changes (the even power at \(4\) does not): \(g\) has a local maximum at \(q=3\) and a local minimum at \(p=-12\). Hence \(|p+q|=|-12+3|=9.\)
